report:
**Conclusion**
Whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy is an effective **complementary measure** for reducing fracture risk, though current clinical evidence supports it primarily as an supportive therapy rather than a standalone cure.

**Key Findings from Research:**
* **Preserving Bone Mineral Density (BMD):** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses show that low-magnitude, high-frequency WBV modestly increases or maintains BMD, particularly in the lumbar spine and femoral neck of postmenopausal women (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-022-06556-y, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13018-016-0357-2).
* **Fall Prevention:** Falls are the leading cause of osteoporotic fractures. WBV strengthens lower-body muscles and improves postural balance, thereby reducing overall fall frequency (https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/7/12/e018342).
* **Direct Fracture Reduction:** While studies indicate WBV can lower fracture risk by improving bone health and reducing falls, direct high-certainty evidence demonstrating substantial fracture prevention from WBV alone remains limited compared to standard pharmacological treatments (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139).

In summary, WBV therapy is safe and beneficial for slowing bone loss and improving balance, making it a valuable addition to standard osteoporosis care, but it should be combined with physician-recommended lifestyle changes and medical therapies.

**Sources:**
* https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/7/12/e018342
* https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-022-06556-y
* https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13018-016-0357-2
* https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139
